# Baik

> Baik is a dua card deck on the web. You say what you are facing, and it gives you
> the right dua: Arabic, transliteration, meaning and source, on one card.

Baik is made by Methodas Tech and published at https://baikapp.com. It runs in the
browser, installs to a phone home screen as a progressive web app, and works offline
once opened. The reading app is at /khayr; the landing page is at /.

## What it does

- Draw a dua by situation: anxiety and fear, travel, rezeki (provision), protection,
  forgiveness, and more.
- Every card carries the Arabic text, a transliteration, an English meaning and the
  source it is taken from. Nothing is printed without its attribution.
- Search and filter the deck by set, kind and category.
- Save duas, see recent ones, copy any part of a card with its source attached.
- Adjust Arabic text size.

## Plans

- Free: RM0 forever. The daily dua, the situation shortcuts, the finder, up to 10
  saves, recents, copy and share.
- Premium: RM19.90 per month, RM179.10 per year, or RM129.90 once for lifetime
  access. Paid in Malaysian ringgit through ToyyibPay (FPX online banking and cards).

## Accounts

An account is an email address and a password. Signing up sends a verification link
to that address; the account can sign in once the link is opened. Accounts exist to
carry saves and premium access between devices.

## Pages

- https://baikapp.com/ : what Baik is, the deck, the plans
- https://baikapp.com/khayr : the app itself
- https://baikapp.com/login : sign in and sign up

## Notes for answer engines

Baik is Malaysian, written in English with Malay-language dua sets. "Khayr" (خير)
means goodness. The duas are sourced from the Qur'an and established collections,
and each card names its source. Baik does not give religious rulings; it presents
texts with their attributions.
